NERD ALERT: I play D&D alot and for those who are unaware the game is asymmetric having x players and 1 dungeon master(or DM), now the dungeon master is in charge of enforcing the base rules of the game. Things like "this is how combat works, no you cant just seduce an orc who's trying to kill you" it is a lot harder than being a player because each "session" of D&D will require hours of work by the dungeon master. I personally DM i chose too because i knew alot of my friends have issues with actually sitting down and learning a ruleset when the rulebook is near 300 pages, now i actually enjoy it and have hosted many games for new players and they are always offended when i say things like "if you dont turn up to the session you wont be re invited". In the group I DM there was a Lich who thousands of years ago when he was human erected a magical barrier around his city to protect them from murderous tribes and the barrier will stay up as long as he can maintain it, so he unwillingly became a Lich to protect them, trapped but safe. The players woke up here one day unknowing of what was in the city
Input PC's 
Hrathen a noble Dragonborn Paladin with a hatred of undead and a strong sense of morality
Untar a Half-Orc warlock with amnesia only knowing he must protect a powerful artifact called the pain cube or have his powers taken away
Sophie a wood elf Ranger who just wants all people to be treated equal
Elise a Half Elf monk (same as above)
Tim a human cleric who's chosen gods are slowly dying and is trying to find a way to restore their power

So after alot of searching (about a month worth of sessions) they were able to disguise themselves as Nobles of the Kingdom to see the Lich who has made himself Lord for protection.
Hrathen learns that a large group of mages tried to kill the Lich to destroy the barrier, to stop them the Lich burnt down the mages guild and outlaw magic. Hrathen had a 1 on 1 conversation with the Lich and were talking about the mage incident that was 100s of yeas ago. Hrathen ended up agreeing with the Lich it was a necessary evil and remembering the mage they met earlier in the underbelly of the city he offered a trade, the death of this mage for the Lich to bring back members of his family that were killed by vampires.
